name: SIA Project 25 26
description:
In the Municipality of Turin, a system called Participium is being developed — an information 
system that enables citizen participation in the management of urban environments. It allows 
citizens to interact with the public administration by reporting inconveniences and malfunctions 
found in the city (e.g., potholes in the asphalt, sidewalks with architectural barriers, garbage in the 
streets, broken streetlights, etc.). An example of a similar information system is IRIS in Venice: 
https://iris.sad.ve.it/. The system, once developed, will be made available as open-source 
software to all Italian public administrations through the portal https://developers.italia.it/.

A. REPORTS 
Citizens can submit reports only if they have registered in the system with a username, first name, 
and last name. Once the registration is received, the user gets an email with a confirmation link. 
The registration becomes valid, and the user can use the system only after confirming through 
that link. Once registered, a citizen can submit reports by selecting a point on the map of Turin 
(which will be saved with latitude and longitude values) and filling in a problem form with the 
following mandatory fields: title, textual description, category (chosen from a predefined list). It is 
also mandatory to attach one or more photos (up to 3 per report, with each photo stored with its 
file path on the server). The possible problem categories are: 
• Waterworks – Drinking water 
• Architectural Barriers 
• Sewerage 
• Public Lighting 
• Waste 
• Road Signs and Traffic Lights 
• Roads and Urban Furniture 
• Public Green Areas and Playgrounds 
• Other 
After entering all the information and the pictures, the system asks the citizen whether they want 
the report to be anonymous (the name will not appear in the public list of all reports).  

B. REPORT LIFECYCLE 
Once submitted, the report is in the “Pending Approval” state until the Organization Office of the 
Municipality of Turin performs a preliminary review of citizen reports, marking them as accepted 
or rejected. The possible states for a report are: Pending Approval, In Progress, Work in Progress, 
Suspended, Rejected. After approval, accepted reports move to the “In Progress” state, at which 
point they are assigned to the technical office responsible, based on the problem category. Once 
the intervention is planned, the state changes to “Work in Progress”, indicating that the issue 
resolution has started. In some cases, for organizational or technical reasons, the report can be 
set to “Suspended”, awaiting further evaluation or resources. When the problem is solved, the 
technical office updates the status and closes the report. In case of rejection, a written explanation 
from the Organization Office is mandatory (see next section).  
If the intervention must be carried out by maintenance personnel from an external company (for 
example, Enel X for Public Lighting, or company Y for specific reports based on their content), 
two cases are possible: - Case 1: The company has access to Participium. In this case, the technical office assigns the 
report to users from the corresponding company. External maintenance personnel can move the 
report from Assigned to In Progress. Staff from the technical office and external maintenance 
workers can exchange information and comments through the report, but these are not visible to 
the reporting citizen (nor to other citizens). Once the work is completed, the external maintainer 
can mark the report as resolved. 
Note: Automatic assignment of all reports in a certain category to the external company 
(bypassing the initial review by the public relations officer of the municipality) is possible only if 
previously configured by the municipal administrator. - Case 2: The company does NOT have access to Participium. In this case, the external company 
updates the technical office outside Participium, and once the problems are solved, a staff 
member from the technical office will manually move the report to the Resolved state. 


C. CITIZEN UPDATES 
To strengthen trust between citizens and institutions, the citizen can receive updates regarding 
their own reports through various channels. First, at every state change, the citizen receives a 
notification on the platform with the corresponding update. Furthermore, municipal operators 
updating reports can send the reporting citizen a message through the platform, to which it can 
reply. The system must allow this functionality to be accessible by external chatbots as well. Each 
time the citizen receives a notification on the platform, they also get an email (this option can be 
disabled in the user settings panel, where they can also upload a personal photo). 
Moreover, after the approval phase, accepted reports immediately become visible on the 
Participium portal: they appear both on an interactive map of Turin, geolocated based on the 
citizen’s selected point, and in a summary table that allows filtering and sorting reports by 
category, status, or date. In both views, the reporter’s name (“anonymous” if that option was 
chosen) and the report title are displayed. Clicking on the title opens a page with the description.  
Even non-registered users can view both the maps and the summary table. Once logged into 
Participium, citizens can follow other citizens’ open reports and receive notifications (following the 
same rules as for their own reports). 


D. STATISTICS 
The system allows viewing public and private statistics. Public statistics are visible in a dedicated 
section of the website and concern the number of reports per category, and trends over day, week, 
or month. They are also visible to non-registered users. In the private section, accessible only to 
administrators, it is possible to view, in addition to the public statistics, charts and tables.

highLevelGoals: Enable citizens to register and submit detailed reports about urban issues through a user-friendly interface, ensuring their active participation in urban management.
Enhance the efficiency of the review and management of citizen reports by municipal operators to ensure timely approvals and effective resolutions of urban issues.
Provide external maintenance personnel with the necessary tools and access to manage and resolve reported issues effectively, ensuring accountability and communication with municipal operators.
Enable municipal administrators to configure system settings and oversee the assignment of reports to ensure proper management and accountability in urban issue resolution.
Allow non-registered users to access and view reports and statistics to foster transparency and encourage community engagement in urban management.
lowLevelGoals: Allow citizens to create a new account by providing a username, name, and email through a registration API.
Enable citizens to confirm their email address through an email confirmation API after registration.
Allow citizens to submit a new report detailing an urban issue through a form submission API.
Enable citizens to upload images or videos related to their report using a media upload API.
Allow citizens to view the status of their submitted reports through a report status retrieval API.
Allow citizens to follow specific reports to receive updates on their status through a follow report API.
Enable the system to send notifications to citizens via email or platform notifications when the status of their report changes through a notification API.
Allow municipal operators to access and review submitted reports through a report retrieval API.
Enable municipal operators to update the status of a report (e.g., in review, resolved) through a report status update API.
Allow municipal operators to assign a report to external maintenance personnel through an assignment API.
Enable external maintenance personnel to view reports assigned to them through a report assignment retrieval API.
Allow external maintenance personnel to update the resolution status of a report through a resolution status update API.
Enable external maintenance personnel to exchange comments with municipal operators through a comments API.
Enable municipal administrators to modify system configuration settings through a system configuration API.
Allow municipal administrators to access and view statistics related to reports through a statistics retrieval API.
Allow non-registered users to view public reports through a public report retrieval API.
Enable non-registered users to access statistics on community engagement through a community engagement statistics API.

branch_001.rationale:
The original High-Level Goal 'Facilitate Citizen Reporting' accurately captures the primary functional intention of the Citizens actor as described in the project documentation (Sections A and C). The goal encompasses registration, submission of detailed reports (including location, description, category, and photos), and the implicit tracking of these reports. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Facilitate citizen engagement in urban issue reporting and tracking' is semantically equivalent but slightly more verbose. The original goal is specific enough to distinguish it from the 'Non-registered Users' goal (which focuses on viewing/transparency) and the 'Municipal Operators' goal (which focuses on review/resolution). It is not too generic, narrow, or incorrectly scoped. Therefore, it should be kept. The current Low-Level Goals (LLGs) adequately cover the essential capabilities required by the parent High-Level Goal 'Facilitate Citizen Reporting'. The parent goal explicitly requires citizens to 'register' and 'submit detailed reports'. 

1. **Registration**: Covered by 'Register Citizen' (llg_001) and 'Confirm Email' (llg_002), which aligns with the documentation stating registration requires username, name, and email confirmation.
2. **Submission**: Covered by 'Submit Report' (llg_003) and 'Attach Media to Report' (llg_004). The documentation mandates title, description, category, location, and photos. While the specific fields (category, location) are not explicitly named in the LLG descriptions, 'Submit Report' and 'Attach Media' are sufficient atomic capabilities to encompass the submission process. The evaluator guidelines state that 'Technical/API wording alone is not an error when the decomposition is complete' and 'Different granularity... are not material defects'. The core capability of submitting the report with its details is present.
3. **Tracking/Updates**: The parent goal mentions 'ensuring their active participation', which implies tracking. 'View Submitted Reports' (llg_005) and 'Follow Report' (llg_006) cover the citizen's ability to track their own reports and follow others, as described in section C.

No essential capability explicitly required by the parent HLG is absent. The LLGs do not contradict the documentation. Capabilities belonging to sibling HLGs (e.g., review, resolution, admin configuration) are correctly excluded.

branch_004.rationale: All the low-level goals focus on providing municipal administrators with tools to manage, monitor, and optimize the handling of reports, ensuring that they can set parameters, view assignments, adjust responsibilities, and resolve issues effectively.

The original High-Level Goal 'Empower System Configuration and Report Management' accurately captures the two main functional responsibilities of the Municipal Administrators described in the project description: configuring system settings (specifically mentioned in Section B regarding automatic assignment rules) and overseeing report management (implied by the actor description and the need to manage the workflow). The bottom-up reconstruction is more generic ('Enhance efficiency...') and less specific about the actual functional scope (configuration and assignment oversight). The original goal is supported by the text, correctly scoped to the actor, and distinct from the goals of Municipal Operators (who handle the day-to-day review and assignment execution) and Citizens. Therefore, it should be kept. The current Low-Level Goals (LLGs) adequately cover the core responsibilities of the parent High-Level Goal (HLG) 'Empower System Configuration and Report Management'. 

1. **System Configuration**: LLG_001 ('Configure System Settings') addresses the requirement for administrators to set parameters. The documentation explicitly mentions that 'Automatic assignment... is possible only if previously configured by the municipal administrator.' This configuration capability is captured by LLG_001.

2. **Report Management/Oversight**: The HLG requires overseeing the assignment of reports.
